title: Semantic Code Search Engine with Tree-Sitter AST Chunking & Vector Retrieval
problem: Software engineers frequently navigate large unfamiliar codebases using literal string searches or regex queries, which consistently fail to discover code with differing naming conventions or abstract conceptual implementations. Traditional lexical search cannot capture syntactic structures or natural language semantic intent. This project builds an intelligent semantic code search engine in Python. The system parses source code files into structural abstract syntax tree (AST) chunks using Tree-sitter, computes dense vector representations using open-source code embedding models, stores vectors in a local Qdrant vector database, and serves natural language search queries through a FastAPI backend combining dense semantic retrieval with sparse BM25 keyword matching via Reciprocal Rank Fusion.
use_cases: Developer onboarding tools enabling natural language discovery of repository business logic
Automated duplicate and near-duplicate function identification across enterprise monorepositories
IDE contextual code discovery plugins matching user task descriptions to existing library utilities
hard_parts: Extracting structurally coherent function and class blocks across multiple programming languages using Tree-sitter AST queries
Selecting and quantizing code embedding models to execute inference within standard CPU RAM limits
Implementing hybrid retrieval combining dense vector similarity with sparse BM25 scoring via Reciprocal Rank Fusion
Maintaining sub-200 millisecond end-to-end search query latency across indexed repositories exceeding 25,000 code functions
screener_signals: Clean Python implementation separating AST parsing, embedding inference, vector indexing, and FastAPI endpoints
Evaluation benchmark evaluating Recall@10 and Mean Reciprocal Rank (MRR) across 100 natural language query test pairs
Anti-fake verification script indexing a dynamic code snippet with unique variable names and retrieving it via pure semantic intent

components.name: Tree-Sitter AST Extractor
components.purpose: Parses Python, Go, and JavaScript source files into clean function and class AST nodes with metadata

components.name: Code Embedding Pipeline
components.purpose: Transforms structural code chunks and docstrings into 384-dimensional dense vectors using all-MiniLM-L6-v2

components.name: Qdrant Hybrid Vector Index
components.purpose: Stores dense embeddings and BM25 sparse payloads, executing cosine similarity search via HNSW graphs

components.name: FastAPI Semantic Search Gateway
components.purpose: Exposes search REST endpoints, combines dense and sparse ranks via Reciprocal Rank Fusion, and returns formatted code snippets

architecture.data_flow: Source code repositories are scanned by the Tree-Sitter AST Extractor; function definitions, parameters, and docstrings are extracted into structured code chunks; the Code Embedding Pipeline generates dense embeddings for each chunk; embeddings and text metadata are indexed into local Qdrant collections; client natural language queries enter FastAPI; the query is embedded and evaluated against Qdrant dense vectors and BM25 keywords; Reciprocal Rank Fusion merges ranked results; ranked code snippets with syntax highlighting return to the user.
architecture.enforcement_mechanism: Structural AST node boundaries preventing arbitrary line truncation; cosine similarity distance thresholds filtering low-relevance results.

prerequisites: Proficiency in Python programming, type annotations, and asynchronous FastAPI development
Understanding of vector embeddings, cosine distance, vector search databases, and text chunking

environment.gpu: None required (purely CPU-bound quantized model inference)
environment.cost: $0 (fully open-source software stack and local embedding weights)
environment.accounts_keys_quotas: No external cloud accounts, paid services, or API keys required
environment.reference_environment: Local 4-core CPU with Python 3.11 and Qdrant local storage or Docker installed
environment.fallback_path: In-memory FAISS or Numpy cosine similarity matrix if Qdrant binary cannot be initialized

riskiest_component.name: High Embedding Inference Latency on Local CPU
riskiest_component.fallback: Leverage quantized ONNX runtime for embedding models (e.g. all-MiniLM-L6-v2 ONNX) to cut CPU latency by 3x
